answer:
Set up a classic two-dimensional dam-break simulation using the interFoam solver.
Create the computational domain with dimensions 0.584 meters in length, 0.584 meters in height, and 0.01 meters in depth along the z-axis.
Generate a structured mesh using blockMesh with one cell thickness in the z-direction.
Assign the front and back boundaries the empty patch type to enforce two-dimensional flow.
Assign the bottom, left, and right boundaries as no-slip walls.
Assign the top boundary as an open atmosphere boundary using totalPressure for pressure and pressureInletOutletVelocity for velocity.
Initialize the water column in the bottom-left corner with a width of 0.146 meters and a height of 0.292 meters using setFields.
Set alpha.water to 1 inside the water column and 0 elsewhere in the domain.
Set the fluid properties in constant/transportProperties with water density of 1000 kg/m3, water kinematic viscosity of 1e-6 m2/s, air density of 1 kg/m3, air kinematic viscosity of 1.48e-5 m2/s, and surface tension of 0.07 kg/s2.
Configure gravity in constant/g to act in the negative y-direction at 9.81 m/s2.
Set application to interFoam in system/controlDict.
Set startTime to 0 and endTime to 1.0 seconds in system/controlDict.
Configure adjustable time stepping based on a maximum Courant number of 0.5.
Set writeControl to adjustableRunTime with a writeInterval of 0.05 seconds.
